output.summary: Deciduous hardwood trees and shrubs native to Eurasia and North America, especially northern temperate and boreal regions. Their bark has long horizontal markings and often peels into thin, papery plates. The inner bark can serve as emergency food, while the sap can be drunk or made into syrup and birch beer.
output.edibilityNote: Inner bark may be eaten raw or dried into flour; sap is drunk or made into syrup and birch beer.
